panel-amber-glow-core-dark.displayName: Digit Glow Core (dark only; transparent in light)

panel-amber-glow-dark.displayName: Digit Glow Halo (dark only; transparent in light)

title.purpose: The page's h1 only, in Inter.

digit-readout.purpose: Each card's headline USD price — shares Title's size/weight but renders in the mono face with tabular-nums, since it is instrument data, not a heading.

headline.purpose: Each card's coin name (h2) — one step below Title/Digit Readout, a real shift from the prior world where card name and price shared one size.

body.purpose: Page subtitle, button labels, filter input text, banner/empty-state copy.

label.purpose: Coin symbol, BTC sub-price, badge text, the delta chip's 'recent' caption — mono, for column alignment.

shadows.name: chassis-panel
shadows.purpose: Ambient, resting-state card depth — a bright top lip plus a soft inset shadow. Subtle in light mode, clearly visible in dark mode. Not a hover-triggered effect.

shadows.name: panel-fastener
shadows.purpose: Drag handle's countersunk-mount read, distinct from the flat square icon buttons beside it.

shadows.name: digit-glow
shadows.purpose: Two-layer glow on a lit digit-tube readout — tight near-opaque core plus wide soft halo. Both glow tokens are transparent in light mode, so this renders as plain amber text there with no glow at all.

shadows.name: sparkline-end-dot-glow
shadows.value: SVG filter: feGaussianBlur stdDeviation=1.5 + feMerge over SourceGraphic, per-instance useId()-scoped id
shadows.purpose: Glow on the sparkline's terminal point only, in the trend's status color.

motion.name: digit-crossfade
motion.value: @keyframes digit-crossfade 260ms ease-out (opacity 0.2->1, blur(2px)->blur(0)), gated under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference
motion.purpose: Fires once when a card's displayed price actually changes value (useValueChangeFlash) — the signature 'nixie tube physical digit changeover' interaction. Never fires on mount or on a poll tick that didn't move the price.

motion.name: drag-transform
motion.purpose: Card position animates during drag-and-drop reorder; dropped entirely under reduced motion so the drop still lands, just instantly.

motion.name: refresh-spin
motion.purpose: RefreshCw icon spins while a refresh is in flight; gated since the 'Refreshing…' label already carries the state without it.

motion.name: lamp-color-transition
motion.purpose: Staleness lamp's tier color change. Deliberately NOT gated by motion-safe — a color transition isn't the spatial movement reduced motion asks apps to remove.

motion.name: card-border-hover
motion.purpose: Card/button/input border shifts to panel-amber/40-60 on hover — replaces the prior world's hover-shadow elevation step entirely.

components.css: .ds-card { background: #17191d; border: 1px solid #2b2e34; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 16px; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.05), inset 0 -1px 6px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.5); } .ds-card:hover { border-color: rgba(255,167,38,0.4); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-card { transition: border-color 150ms ease; } } .ds-card-header { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; margin-bottom: 16px; position: relative; } .ds-card-logo { width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #2b2e34; } .ds-card-name { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; color: #e8e9eb; line-height: 1.3; margin: 0; } .ds-card-symbol { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; color: #9a9ea6; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-fastener { margin-left: auto; background: transparent; border: 1px solid #2b2e34; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 10px; color: #9a9ea6; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.5); } .ds-fastener:hover { border-color: rgba(255,167,38,0.4); color: #ffa726; } .ds-digit-readout { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 600; color: #ffa726; text-shadow: 0 0 2px rgba(255,167,38,0.9), 0 0 16px rgba(255,167,38,0.55); } .ds-card-btc { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #9a9ea6; margin-top: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button (Refresh)
components.description: The system's only button style — chassis background, hairline border, amber hover/focus.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: #ffffff; color: #0f1115; border: 1px solid #dfe2e6; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 6px 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 400; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: rgba(154,77,0,0.4); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #9a4d00; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-ghost:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Staleness Badge (Live)
components.description: Pill badge + lamp dot signaling data freshness. The lamp dot uses a component-scoped literal color set (green/amber/red/gray), not the shared STATUS_COLOR tokens the sparkline/delta chip use — see DESIGN.md's Do's and Don'ts on why this isn't promoted into a second general-purpose status source.

components.name: Filter Input
components.description: The page's single text filter, with a leading search icon.
components.css: .ds-input-wrap { position: relative; max-width: 20rem; } .ds-input-icon { position: absolute; left: 12px; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); color: #6b7076; pointer-events: none; } .ds-input-filter { width: 100%; border: 1px solid #dfe2e6; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 6px 12px 6px 36px; font-size: 0.875rem; color: #0f1115; background: #ffffff; } .ds-input-filter::placeholder { color: #6b7076; } .ds-input-filter:focus { border-color: rgba(154,77,0,0.6); } .ds-input-filter:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #9a4d00; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
This build supersedes "The Instrument Panel" (the prior grayscale, no-accent world). The thesis held — the numbers are still the interface — but the execution committed to a single physical metaphor: each price is a glowing digit-tube reading on a brushed-steel chassis, not a flat number in a bordered card. One warm amber is the system's single committed signal — the instrument's own light source — rendered as tabular-mono digits that go from an unlit, muted tube (no rate yet) to a lit, glowing one (a real reading in hand) the instant data arrives.

The chassis material is genuinely dual-scene, not a single palette with a dark-mode filter over it. Dark mode is the native scene: a dim room where a two-layer text-shadow (a near-opaque core plus a soft wide halo) makes the amber price read as an actual light source, and the card itself gets a real inset-shadow chassis depth against a near-black floor. Light mode is not that scene inverted — it follows real trading-platform convention (Binance-style): crisp near-white throughout, hierarchy carried by hairline dividers and typography, and the amber token retunes to a deep burnt tone with its glow tokens literally set to transparent, because a daylight scene cannot sustain a dominant glow the way a dim room can.
keyCharacteristics: One committed accent (amber) marks affordance and 'a real reading exists'; it never carries market-direction or freshness meaning — those stay in a separate status palette.
Dark mode is the hero scene for the amber glow (two-layer text-shadow); light mode is a genuinely different, glow-off reading of the same object, not an inversion.
The digit-readout tube is typography-only until a --lit modifier is applied on a truthy rate — an unlit tube is never mistaken for 'a reading that was never taken.'
Depth is now ambient (inset chassis shadows on the card and drag-handle-as-fastener), not interactive-only hover feedback the way the prior world's single hover-shadow was.
Radius language simplified to two steps: rounded-lg for every container/control, rounded-full for anything meant to read as a dot, mount, or lamp.

rules.name: The Single-Amber Rule
rules.body: Exactly one warm accent exists in this system. It marks 'this is interactive' (hover, focus) and 'this is a live reading' (a lit digit tube). It never marks trend direction or freshness — those stay in the separate status/lamp vocabulary, so a glance can't confuse 'the instrument is on' with 'the market moved.'

rules.name: The Native-Scene Rule
rules.body: The amber glow is a dark-mode-native phenomenon: --panel-amber-glow and --panel-amber-glow-core are literally transparent in :root. Light mode is a deliberately different, glow-off reading of the same instrument, never a dimmed copy of the dark-mode value.

rules.name: The Muted-Line Rule
rules.body: A trend sparkline's line is always the muted status hue; only its terminal point ever takes the direction-specific status color.

rules.name: The Instrument-Reading Rule
rules.body: Anything that is a live numeric reading off the dashboard (the USD price, the BTC rate, the coin code) renders in the mono face with tabular-nums. Anything that is prose or a heading renders in Inter. A component never mixes the two within a single value.

rules.name: The Ambient-Depth Rule
rules.body: Chassis depth (the inset highlight/shadow pairing) is a resting-state material property of cards and the drag handle, not a hover-triggered elevation change. Hover communicates interactivity through the amber border instead.

rules.name: The Two-Layer Glow Rule
rules.body: Wherever the amber accent glows (digit tubes, sparkline end-dot), it uses a tight near-opaque core plus a separate wide soft halo — never a single shadow layer. A single soft shadow was tried and reviewed as reading like 'bold colored text,' not a light source.

dos: Do spend the amber accent only on 'this is interactive' or 'this is a live reading' — hover borders, focus rings, and lit digit tubes.
Do keep trend/freshness meaning in the separate status/lamp vocabulary, never in amber.
Do apply the two-layer glow (core + halo) wherever the amber accent needs to read as a light source; never a single shadow layer.
Do gate spatial motion (digit cross-fade, drag-settle transform) under prefers-reduced-motion, and keep color-only transitions (the staleness lamp) ungated.
Do render a coin with no rate yet as an unlit, plain-color digit tube — never fabricate a 'reading.'
Do give every interactive control a visible amber :focus-visible outline.
donts: Don't use amber for market-direction or freshness state — that would collide 'the instrument is on' with 'the market moved.'
Don't apply the digit-tube glow in light mode — the glow tokens are transparent there by design.
Don't add a shadow step to card hover — hover communicates via the amber border, not elevation; depth is already ambient at rest.
Don't color a sparkline's full line by trend direction — only its end-dot carries the signal color.
Don't add a filled/primary-style button; every button in this system is an outline/chassis control.
Don't treat the StalenessBadge's literal lamp colors as a second general-purpose status token source — they are scoped to that one component; new state-driven UI should route through STATUS_COLOR.
